parts:
Robin:

Congrats on working hard (6118km of effort) in the first year of your stu=
dy, and
closely reading Chapter 7 of Buckland et al. (2001). You raise a good po=
int
about the magnitude of your estimate of b. You could compute b yet anoth=
er
way, using eqn. 7.2 (and that would also show you how much of b is coming=
from
variability between transects and how much coming from uncertainty in f(0=
)).

But if you take a step back and look at your conclusions; putting in 6000=
km of
effort you get a cv of 0.13, and if you raise that effort to 9500-10500km=
of
effort, you can bring your cv down to 0.10. Recognize that squeezing a c=
v from
0.15 to 0.10 is much much harder than moving the cv from 0.30 to 0.25 (a =
graph
of cv vs effort becomes increasingly 'flat' as effort gets larger). So s=
etting
aside your concern about b, it makes sense that you'll need to work reall=
y hard
to shrink those last few cv units.

Quoting Robin W Hunnewell <rhu...@mac.com>:

year.

from an
> > operational year are in hand, these can be used to estimate b in order =
to

> > Total line length (Lo) from my first year of line transect surveys was =
6118

Then I did

> >
> > Finally my question: assuming I've done it correctly and est'd b and L =
values
